verdict: APPROVE as a distinct startup-only mode. The classification is honest: every label and record says physical_input_proven=false / STARTUP_ONLY_NO_INPUT_PROOF, and exit 0 means only 'readiness observed and owned child reaped'. The genuine PTY I/O, XKB-only input path and owned cleanup are byte-identical to the qualified revision-2 terminal. Q1 and Q2 are qualification rules, not code defects.

diff_vs_qualified_rev2.files: Only Cargo.toml (package name), Cargo.lock (root package name only; every other line identical), README.md and src/main.rs differ from the revision-2 set (79c6c89f). grid.rs, keys.rs, negotiation.rs, protocol.rs, pty.rs (9edf5cb8), render.rs and the font are identical. The original client-terminal source is unchanged.
main_rs: Title 'Chonkstep — native keyboard startup (input unverified)' (the app_id org.darwinlab.terminal is unchanged).
READY becomes 'DL12_NATIVE_STARTUP_READY <n> origin=native_input_unverified pty=ready keymap=xkb_v1 focus=own_surface frame=ready physical_input_proven=false'.

The strict-response announcement becomes the diagnostic-only 'DL12_NATIVE_STARTUP_REPLY_OBSERVED <n> source=pty_shell physical_input_proven=false'. The recognizer is unchanged and can only fire on real post-READY PTY bytes.
result.json origin becomes native_input_unverified and adds qualification STARTUP_ONLY_NO_INPUT_PROOF and native_physical_typing_proven false; the cleanup and session fields are unchanged.

Exit gate: after cleanup.complete, it requires session.ready instead of session.response; then 'DL12_NATIVE_STARTUP_DONE <n> readiness=observed physical_input_proven=false cleanup=reaped'. The error prefix is renamed.

verified: Classification: READY derives from the compositor's seat (keymap, focus, neutral modifiers), the PTY exec boundary plus output, SSD and a completed frame. A compositor sends keymap and focus whether or not any physical keyboard ever reports, so READY says nothing about native keyboard function, and the labels say exactly that.

Genuine I/O preserved: only master reads feed the grid, records and recognizer; only XKB-translated wl_keyboard presses feed TX, written only after READY and while the shell owns the foreground. No host command or text is inserted (no injection path exists in the diff).

Keyboard-only seat compatibility: the wl_seat handler requests a keyboard when capabilities contain Keyboard and never needs a pointer (main.rs:171), so it suits Grok's keyboard-only seat. Window creation still requires an advertised seat.
Cleanup unchanged: owned TERM/KILL with bounded reap, idempotent, always before result.json; exit 0 requires cleanup.complete.
Tests re-run here: 26/26 OK (cargo test --offline --locked, scratch target).

qualification_rules.text: Exit 0 also happens if the shell dies after READY (session ends on pty_eof, cleanup reaps an already-exited child). A startup qualification must additionally require from result.json session.pty_eof false, window_closed false, term_signal false (or a supervisor-sent TERM recorded as such), and the raw child wait status recorded. DONE alone is not enough.

Text before READY and duplicate presses are hard failures, carried over from revision 2. With a physical keyboard, a key pressed during boot turns the startup run into a failure; that is fail-closed and acceptable for unattended runs, but say so in the packet. A press during the run is real input going to the PTY, and the transcript records it; it must not be confused with host-origin input (the TX ledger must end at the launcher command, with no PDSerialHID lines).

Nothing in this mode is physical-typing evidence, including REPLY_OBSERVED. The window does not display the nonce, so a human cannot produce the strict reply without a separately reviewed physical-typing procedure.

notes.text: Consider a distinct app_id (for example org.darwinlab.terminal-native-startup) so compositor logs and pixels distinguish it from the host-qualified terminal; the title already distinguishes them.

scope: Read-only source review plus host tests in a scratch target. No hardware or edits.
